including the charge-sheet, of Criminal Case No. 86 of 2018, arising out of Case Crime No. 29 of 2017, under Sections-498-A, 323, 506 IPC, P. S. Mahila Thana, district-Gautam Budh Nagar,

sentences.text: 1 3. learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the allegations levelled against the applicant are wholly false and no prima facie case is made out against the applicant.
The allegation that marriage of victim with the son of applicant has taken place on 26.6.2009, is wholly false.
There is no documentary evidence to prove the said marriage.

Learned counsel submitted that the son of applicant was already married and no marriage has taken place with victim and in fact, it was a live-in-relationship between victim and son of applicant and thus, the victim does not fall within the ambit of wife and the instant complaint under Section 498A IPC would not be maintainable at the instance of victim / opposite party no. 2.
Further, at the time of alleged date of marriage, applicant was in Uttarakhand, where she used to work and she was residing at Roorkie.

Applicnt has shifted to Noida after 16.8.2015 and she has resided in Orchid Avenue Colony, whereas informant was residing at Bango Palm Colony along with Dr. Avinash Prakash Agarwal in live-in-relationship.
During investigation Section 495 IPC has already been deleted.
There is long and undue delay in lodging of the first information report and charge-sheet has been submitted in a routine manner against the accused persons.
Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that no prima facie case is made out against the applicant.

Learned counsel for applicant has placed reliance upon following case laws:-
(i) Shivcharan Lal Verma and another Versus State of M.P.; 2002 (3) Supreme 168;
(ii) P. Shivkumar and others Versus State represented by Police etc.; 2023 0 Supreme (SC) 875; and (iii) Suman Sharma Versus State of Chhattisgarh ; 2024 0 Supreme (Chh) 13.
4.

sentences.text: learned AGA has opposed the application and submitted that the informant / victim has clearly alleged that her marriage with son of the applicant has taken place on 26.6.2009 in a temple and out of that marriage, she has a six years old child.
Victim has made clear allegations that she was being harassed by the accused persons on account of dowry.
Victim has also alleged that the son of the applicant has married with her by concealing his first marriage.
It was submitted that in view of the allegations levelled against the accused persons and material on record, a prima facie case is made out against the accused persons, including the applicant.
5. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

6. The legal position on the issue of quashing of criminal proceedings is well-settled that the jurisdiction to quash a complaint, FIR or a charge-sheet should be exercised sparingly and only in exceptional cases.

However, where the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and material on record even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused, the charge-sheet may be quashed in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

In well celebrated judgement reported in AIR 1992 SC 605 State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal, Supreme Court has carved out certain guidelines, wherein FIR or proceedings may be quashed but cautioned that the power to quash FIR or proceedings should be exercised sparingly and that too in the rarest of rare cases.

sentences.text: It has been held that if a prima facie case is made out disclosing ingredients of the offence, court should not quash the charge sheet/complaint.
It is equally well settled that at this stage questions of fact cannot be examined and a mini trial cannot be held.

7. In the instant matter as per prosecution version, the marriage of opposite party no. 2 with son of applicant has taken place on 26.6.2009 in Sanatan Dharma Temple in Delhi and after marriage informant / opposite party no. 2 was harassed on account of dowry.
It was also alleged that the son of applicant was already a married person and he has married with informant / opposite party no. 2 by concealing his first marriage.

The case of the applicant is that there had been no legal marriage between her son, namely, Avinash Prakash Agarwal and informant / opposite party no. 2 and in fact,
Avinash Prakash Agarwal was married with one Shweta Agarwal and in the year 2012 Dr. Avinash Agarwal has got divorce from his wife Shweta Agarwal and the informant / victim had lived in live-in-relationship with Dr. Avinash Prakash Agarwal.
It was alleged that the son of applicant has never solemnized marriage with informant / opposite party no. 2.

Thus, the main contention raised on behalf of the applicant is that there had been no lawful marriage between the son of applicant and informant / opposite party no. 2 and thus, no offence under Section 498-A IPC would be made out against the applicant.
8.

In case of Shivcharan Lal Verma and another (supra) the marriage of victim with her alleged husband was found null and void and thus, the conviction of husband under Section 498-A IPC was set aside by the High Court and that order was upheld by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
That matter pertains to appeal after conviction.
Similarly, in case of P. Shiv Kumar and others (supra) the conviction under Section 498-A IPC was set aside by following the law down in the case of Shivcharan Lal Verma (supra).
Similar proposition of law has been laid down in case of Suman Sharma (supra).
All these three cases pertains to the matter of conviction / acquittal after trial.
None of the said case pertain to quashing of the proceedings under Section 482 CrPC.
As mentioned above, in jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC, this Court cannot hold a mini trial and questions of facts cannot be examined at this stage.
In the present matter whether the marriage of son of applicant with informant / opposite party no. 2 was lawful or they were living in live-in-relationship

,
can only be decided during trial on the basis of the evidence led by the parties.
At this stage, only it is to be seen whether a prima facie case is made out or not.

The informant / victim has clearly stated that she was married with Dr. Avinash Prakash Agarwal, who is son of applicant, and that she was harassed by the accused persons, including applicant, on account of dowry.

Victim / informant has further alleged that out of that marriage she has a six years old child and that she was assaulted by the accused persons, including the applicant, and later on, when she talked with applicant on phone,
she has made a demand for Rs. 10,000,00/- (Ten lacs).

9. In view of the allegations made in the first information report and the material collected during investigation, it cannot be said that no prima facie case is made out against the applicant, who as per prosecution, is the mother-in-law of the victim / opposite party no. 2.
The above referred case laws do not provide help to the applicant at this stage.

So far as the arguments that applicant was working in Uttarakhand and she resided at Roorkee and when she came to reside at NOIDA, she has resided Smt.Smt.Indu Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128659513/

sentences.text: 3 separately, are concerned, the same also relate to questions of fact, which cannot be examined at this stage.
The submissions raised by learned counsel for the applicant call for determination of questions of facts, which may adequately be discerned / adjudicated only by the trial Court.
Even the submissions made on the point of law, can also be more appropriately gone into by the trial Court.
Thus, the prayer as made above, is refused.

10. However, the applicant would be at liberty to raise all her contentions before the trial Court at the time of framing of charges or she may file application seeking discharge in accordance with law.
In case, she files an application for discharge within a period of four weeks from today, the same shall be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with law.

It is further directed that four a period of four weeks from today and in case she files application for discharge within the aforesaid period, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant till the disposal of such discharge application, provided she cooperates in early disposal of discharge application.
11. with the aforesaid observations, this application under Section 482 CrPC is disposed of.
